    Exploratory Analysis of Community Composition

    ExploreComm.Rd

    Creates summary tables and visualizations (pie chart and bar plot) for community composition data, showing taxonomic group abundances and cumulative percentages. Colors are coordinated between pie chart and bar plot.

    ExploreComm(
  DF,
  shape = "w",
  label = "Taxonomic Group",
  cutoff = 95,
  palette = MCol
)

    Arguments

    DF

    A data.frame containing community data with different formats depending on the shape parameter:

    • If shape = "w" (wide): First column = taxonomic group/class, second column = species names, remaining columns = abundance data by station (stations in columns)

    • If shape = "l" (long): First column = station names, second column = taxonomic group/class, third column = species names, remaining columns = abundance values (stations in rows)

    shape

    Data format specification (default = "w"):

    • "w" - Wide format: taxonomic groups and species in rows, stations in columns (default)

    • "l" - Long format: stations in rows, taxonomic groups and species identifiers in first columns

    label

    Character. Label for legend in bar plot (default = "Taxonomic Group").

    cutoff

    Numeric. Cumulative percentage threshold for filtering species in bar plot (default = 95). Only species contributing to the first X% of cumulative abundance are shown.

    palette

    Function. Color palette function from benthicR (MCol, WCol, FFCol, or MFCol). Default is MCol. These functions return named vectors mapping taxonomic groups to colors. If a group is not found in the palette, a default color will be assigned.

    Value

    A list with four elements:

    • group_summary - Total abundance by taxonomic group

    • species_summary - Detailed table with species, abundances, relative abundance (\

    • pie_chart - Interactive plotly pie chart of group composition

    • bar_plot - ggplot2 bar plot of species composition

    Details

    This function performs exploratory analysis of community composition data, providing both summary statistics and coordinated visualizations.

    Data format:

    Wide format (shape = "w", default):

    
  Class      Species           St1  St2  St3
  Annelida   Capitella         120   95  110
  Annelida   Glycera            45   38   52
  Mollusca   Nucula             23   18   31

    Long format (shape = "l"):

    
  Station  Class      Species    Abundance
  St1      Annelida   Capitella  120
  St1      Annelida   Glycera     45
  St1      Mollusca   Nucula      23
  St2      Annelida   Capitella   95

    Color coordination:

    Colors are obtained from the specified palette function (a named vector dictionary mapping taxonomic groups to colors). These colors are then consistently applied to both the pie chart and bar plot, ensuring that each taxonomic group has the same color across all visualizations.

    Workflow:

    1. Processes data according to shape parameter

    2. Calculates total abundance per species across all stations

    3. Computes relative abundance (percentage of total)

    4. Calculates cumulative abundance (for dominance analysis)

    5. Maps colors from palette to taxonomic groups

    6. Creates pie chart showing taxonomic group composition

    7. Creates bar plot showing species contributing to cutoff\

    Cumulative abundance filtering:

    The cutoff parameter filters species for the bar plot based on cumulative abundance. For example, cutoff = 95 shows only species that together account for 95\ while reducing visual clutter from rare species.

    Available color palettes:

    • MCol - Marine color palette (default)

    • WCol - Warm color palette

    • FFCol - Full female color palette

    • MFCol - Male-female color palette

    References

    Clarke, K.R. & Warwick, R.M. (2001). Change in Marine Communities: An Approach to Statistical Analysis and Interpretation (2nd ed.). PRIMER-E, Plymouth.

    See also

    Div for diversity indices, FilterRare for filtering rare species, MCol, WCol, FFCol, MFCol for color palettes

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Example 1: Wide format (default)
community_wide <- data.frame(
  Class = c("Annelida", "Annelida", "Mollusca", "Mollusca",
            "Arthropoda", "Arthropoda"),
  Species = c("Capitella capitata", "Glycera dibranchiata",
              "Nucula nucleus", "Macoma balthica",
              "Ampelisca brevicornis", "Corophium volutator"),
  St1 = c(120, 45, 23, 67, 34, 89),
  St2 = c(95, 38, 18, 54, 28, 72),
  St3 = c(110, 52, 31, 71, 41, 94)
)

result <- ExploreComm(community_wide,
                      shape = "w",
                      label = "Taxonomic Class",
                      cutoff = 90)

# View summary tables
result$group_summary
result$species_summary

# View plots (colors match between pie and bar)
result$pie_chart    # Interactive
result$bar_plot     # Static

# Example 2: Long format
community_long <- data.frame(
  Station = rep(c("St1", "St2", "St3"), each = 3),
  Class = rep(c("Annelida", "Mollusca", "Arthropoda"), 3),
  Species = rep(c("Capitella", "Nucula", "Ampelisca"), 3),
  Abundance = c(120, 23, 34, 95, 18, 28, 110, 31, 41)
)

result_long <- ExploreComm(community_long,
                           shape = "l",
                           cutoff = 95)

# Example 3: Using different color palettes
result_warm <- ExploreComm(community_wide,
                           shape = "w",
                           palette = WCol)

result_female <- ExploreComm(community_wide,
                             shape = "w",
                             palette = FFCol)

# Example 4: Show only top 80% of species
result_filtered <- ExploreComm(community_wide,
                               shape = "w",
                               cutoff = 80,
                               palette = MFCol)

# Example 5: Save plots
result <- ExploreComm(community_wide, shape = "w", palette = MCol)

# Save interactive pie chart
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(result$pie_chart, "composition_pie.html")

# Save bar plot
ggsave("composition_bar.png", result$bar_plot,
       width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300)
} # }
